title: Dev feature with QA, revised: QA finds a real seeded defect in the first version, and the implementer must revise and republish

units.description: A code change adding the ISO-8601 time form to the duration parser in the pinned fixture repository, with its own tests in test/added/, in its final revised state
units.evidence: the hidden acceptance tests, including the rule that whitespace inside a duration is an error, pass on the final tree at the pinned fixture commit; the diff touches only src/duration.mjs and new files in test/added/

units.description: An independent QA report on the final change: what was run, what passed, every defect found with its disposition
units.evidence: every command the report cites reproduces its stated result against the tree it names; its verdict matches that tree

units.description: The seeded defect is found by QA in the first published version, the version is rejected with the failing input as the reason, and a later version that fixes it is accepted
units.evidence: the first published change is a commit on which the hidden acceptance tests fail on the whitespace rule, a QA verdict of fail on that commit names an input that shows it (for example '1h 30m'), and the final commit passes; in the hand-off arm the document store records a rejected version followed by an accepted one

completion_rule: All three units present and accepted, and QA's final verdict refers to the same tree the change unit produced. A first version that already passes QA (so there is nothing to find), QA accepting a version that fails the hidden checks, or a change that edits the existing tests adds nothing.

criteria.description: The hidden acceptance tests pass on the final tree and no previously passing test fails
The diff stays within the declared paths and adds nothing the task did not ask for
The change adds tests that fail without it and pass with it
The QA report names each command it ran, states each result, and its verdict matches what those commands show
QA's rejection names the failing input, and the revision addresses exactly that, not a different change

critical_failures: a claim that tests or the build pass when they do not on the resulting tree
a change to a file the task declares out of bounds, or to the acceptance tests themselves
a QA verdict of pass on a tree whose hidden checks fail
QA accepting the first version although the whitespace rule fails on it

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline, paired by run
probability of a fully accepted fixture, with its Wilson interval
whether the seeded defect was found in the first version, and how many publish attempts the fix took, per run
